messages:
alex: Quick RFC follow-up re: private endpoint auth patterns for customer VPCs — peering vs interface endpoints vs sidecar relay. TL;DR: goal is minimal ops surface + strong zero-trust between control plane and customer data plane.

mira: Can you layout the threat model we care about? e.g., cross-account access, lateral movement, exfil over peered links? :thinking:

alex: Main concerns: 1) accidental route exposure across peered meshes, 2) compromised customer instance trying to call control plane RPCs, 3) pressure on our NAT/egress when many small customers flood requests.

jonathan: My quick take: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) gives explicit, non-transitive attachment and SG-level controls — good for least-surprise security. Downsides: ENI/endpoint scalability per AZ and per-account ENI limits. Peering is cheap but transitive routing is a nightmare and needs strict route table discipline.

luis: Also add bandwidth/cost: inter-AZ ENIs for PrivateLink are billed, and you get cross-account data charges. With peering you pay nothing extra but you can't centrally enforce per-customer egress policies easily.

alex: What about a hybrid: PrivateLink for control plane management plane traffic (short, auth-heavy), and peering or VPC-to-VPC for bulk dataplane flows where we need high throughput?

mira: Hybrid makes sense if we can guarantee separation of control vs data plane CIDR ranges and route table hygiene. But that pushes ops complexity onto infra and customers. We should avoid custom per-customer route table templates if possible.

jonathan: Alternative is a per-customer relay (lightweight sidecar relay in regional account) that terminates mTLS and proxies to our control plane over a managed egress channel. Pros: centralizes ENI count, maintains strong auth, simpler customer footprint (one outbound-only peering/NAT). Cons: extra hop + latency.

luis: Sidecar relay idea: customers keep an outbound-only connection to a regional relay (egress-only), so no inbound peering. We enforce mutual TLS with short-lived certs minted by our CA. That avoids transitive routing and reduces SG surface. :+1:

alex: Example policy sketches:
```
# control-plane SG: allow inbound from relays only
sg-controlplane:
  inbound:
    - protocol: tcp
      port: 443
      source: relay-eni-sg
```

mira: Ops questions: who runs the relay? Redwood-managed in customer region (Requires Private subnet + NAT) or customer-run relay image? Managed relays increase our operational blast radius but simplify adoption.

jonathan: If we go managed-relay, we should support two modes: "managed" where we run relay in customer's dedicated account (via partner account setup/installer), and "regional" where customers route to our regional relay via PrivateLink. Both use the same auth model.

luis: Cost model: managed-relay per-customer monthly + per-GB offset. PrivateLink per-endpoint billing. Need to surface clear tradeoffs in the RFC.

infra-bot: infra-bot: noted — created RFC stub: /rfc/private-endpoint-auth-patterns, assigned to @mira for details (link: https://rflink.internal/rfc/1234)

alex: Action items: 1) Mira to draft RFC with threat model + cost/scale table + recommended default (lean: PrivateLink for control, managed relay as opt-in for heavy throughput). 2) Jonathan to prototype relay image + short-lived cert flow. 3) Luis to model per-customer cost for 3 region sizes.

mira: Will start draft today, will include sample diagrams and a small compatibility matrix for peering vs PrivateLink vs relay.

alex: Great. If anyone has prior peering/PL limits we've hit in prod, paste anecdotes here. Otherwise I'll wait for the RFC. :thumbsup:

luis: We hit ENI exhaustion once for a partner integration (account had 250 ENIs in single AZ) — had to ask them to move to multiple AZs. Include that as a note.

jonathan: I'll drop a WIP repo link when prototype exists.

mira: Thanks all — ping me for review if you have example configs.
